close_reason:
Path (a) (doc-only) selected per bead recommendation. Added explicit magic-value documentation to all relevant Option<u64> parameters in jmap-mail-client:

1. EmailGetParams.max_body_value_bytes and EmailParseParams.max_body_value_bytes (mod.rs): documented RFC 8621 §4.1.8/§4.9 'If positive, then...' rule — Some(0) is wire-legal but semantically identical to None (no truncation).

2. email_query, mailbox_query, email_submission_query: added '# Numeric parameter spec magic-values (RFC 8620 §5.5)' or equivalent paragraph documenting position: Some(0) = first item (zero-indexed) and limit: Some(0) = server-default cap, NOT zero results.

3. *_changes methods (email/mailbox/thread/identity/email_submission): documented max_changes spec magic-value semantics — None = server default cap, Some(0) = no client limit, Some(n>0) = at most n entries. Cross-referenced email_changes as the canonical statement to keep doc size bounded.

4. *_query_changes methods (email/mailbox/email_submission): cross-referenced email_changes for max_changes semantics.

NonZeroU64 type upgrade for max_body_value_bytes (the bead's secondary suggestion) is a breaking change and would be a separate workspace-wide decision; deferred.

Bead body did not request workspace propagation to siblings; scoped to mail-client only. If a future bead surfaces the same gap in chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing-client method docs, the same paragraphs apply identically — propagation would be mechanical text duplication.
description:
Several Option<u64> parameters across this crate have RFC-defined magic-value semantics that the docstrings do not surface:

  email.rs:146    email_query(... position: Option<u64>, limit: Option<u64>, ...)
  mailbox.rs:124  mailbox_query(... position: Option<u64>, limit: Option<u64>, ...)
  submission.rs:91 email_submission_query(... position: Option<u64>, limit: Option<u64>, ...)

  email.rs:73     email_changes(..., max_changes: Option<u64>)
  (plus 6 other *_changes methods)

  mod.rs:57       EmailGetParams.max_body_value_bytes: Option<u64>
  mod.rs:275      EmailParseParams.max_body_value_bytes: Option<u64>

RFC 8620 / RFC 8621 magic values:

  - `limit: 0` is permitted but means "an arbitrary limit set by the server", not "no results". RFC 8620 §5.5: "The maximum number of results to return. If null, no limit presumed. The server MAY choose to enforce a maximum..."

  - `position: 0` means "first item" (zero-indexed). RFC 8620 §5.5. Negative values not representable in u64.

  - `max_changes: 0` is meaningful: "no limit" per RFC 8620 §5.2. NOT the same as None (None means "client sets no limit, server applies its default cap"). The 0-vs-None distinction is not documented in the wrapper signatures.

  - `max_body_value_bytes: 0` means "no truncation" per RFC 8621 §4.1.8 ("If positive, then..."). The docstring says "Truncate body values to at most this many bytes" with no mention of the 0-vs-positive special case.

A caller using a typed u64 cannot distinguish "I want zero results" from "I have no preference" from "I want maximum results". The API forces one of:

  (a) Use Option<u64> with None = unset (current), but document 0 explicitly.
  (b) Use Option<NonZeroU64> where 0 is forbidden by the type system, removing the ambiguity (callers wanting "no limit" use None).

Recommendation: (a) for backward compat — add explicit doc lines for each numeric param:

  /// `limit: Some(0)` means "server's default cap" per RFC 8620 §5.5,
  /// not "zero results". Pass `None` to omit the field, or `Some(n)`
  /// where n > 0 for an explicit cap.

For max_body_value_bytes specifically, the 0 case may be safest to upgrade to NonZeroU64 since the spec is explicit that "If positive, then..." — passing 0 is silently equivalent to None, and there is no value to ambiguity here. But that is a breaking change.

Lower priority because most callers will pass realistic positive values and not stumble on the 0 case. Worth surfacing in the docs.

Mark says NO HUMAN — Recommendation: option (a), doc rewrite. NonZeroU64 upgrade is a separate design decision; can be a follow-up bead if desired.
title: Numeric params (position, limit, max_changes, max_body_value_bytes): magic-value semantics not documented
